description: Sector overlay for U.S. banks, non-bank financial technology providers, payment services, broker/dealer-adjacent fintech, lending platforms, and customer financial-data documentation.

metadata.scope: United States-only sector overlay controls for Banking and Fintech. Intended to be used with core_control_library.
metadata.source_note: Source basis revalidated against authoritative U.S. federal statutes, regulations, agency and regulator materials, and applicable model/professional or industry standards available through 2026-08-30. This rule pack remains an evidence-screening control set, not legal advice, and requires qualified legal/compliance review before production reliance. State, territorial, tribal, and local requirements may impose additional obligations.
metadata.external_knowledge_policy: No external knowledge is introduced during document evaluation. Regulatory source mappings live only in this versioned rule pack.

used_for: beneficial ownership at covered financial institutions

primary_sources.name: FTC Safeguards Rule including notification-event requirements

rules.title: BSA/AML program evidence is present
rules.summary: Checks for BSA/AML, CIP, risk-based CDD, beneficial-owner identification/verification under current FinCEN CDD requirements and FIN-2026-R001, sanctions screening, CTR, or SAR evidence. This control concerns financial-institution CDD and must not be read as a Corporate Transparency Act BOI filing requirement for U.S. companies, which are exempt under FinCEN’s August 2026 final rule.

metadata.evidence_expectation: The reviewed document/document set should contain direct textual evidence for this control, or the engine should return missing/review_required according to the rule strategy.
metadata.review_guidance: A qualified U.S. legal/compliance reviewer must confirm applicability, jurisdictional scope, legal sufficiency, and whether absence of textual evidence should be treated as non-compliance.

rules.title: GLBA/customer-information safeguards evidence is present
rules.summary: Checks for a written information security program, risk assessment, customer-information safeguards, service-provider oversight, and—where a notification event occurs—FTC reporting for unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information involving at least 500 consumers no later than 30 days after discovery.
